translations.text: Oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum of Elkosh.
The Lord is a jealous and avenging God. The Lord avenges in anger; the Lord seeks vengeance against his adversaries, and he himself removes his enemies.
The Lord is patient, and his power is great, but the Lord will certainly not acquit. His way is in destruction and upheaval; the wind is his steed, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
He rebukes the sea and dries it up, and he lays waste all the rivers. Bashan and Carmel have dwindled, and all the flowers of Lebanon have faded.
The mountains shook before him, and the hills trembled. The earth was shaken at his presence, together with all its inhabitants.
Who can remain calm before his anger, and who can stand against his furious wrath? His fury melts the powers, and rocks are shattered by him.
The Lord is good to those who wait for him on the day of distress, and he knows those who fear him.
With a flood along the roads he will put an end to those who rise up against him, and darkness will pursue his enemies.
What do you plot against the Lord? He himself will bring an end, and he will not seek the same vengeance a second time in distress.
For they will be laid waste down to their foundations, consumed like a tangled thornbush and like completely dried-out reeds.
From you will come a plot to devise evil against the Lord in defiance.
Thus says the Lord: Concerning the rulers of many waters, they will thus be separated, and news of you will no longer be heard.
And now I will break his rod off you and tear apart your bonds.

The Lord will give a command concerning you: No more offspring will be sown bearing your name. From the house of your god I will wipe out the carved images and the cast images. I will make a grave for you.

For look, swift upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger of good news, who announces peace. Celebrate your festivals, Judah; fulfill your vows, for they will no longer pass through into decay [?]. He has come to an end, wasted away, and been removed.
For one has come up who blows in your face and rescues from distress. Watch the road, brace your waist, and strengthen yourself with great might.
For the Lord has restored the pride of Jacob like the pride of Israel, because plunderers thoroughly plundered them and destroyed his branches.
The weapons of his strength, from among men, mighty men who moved through fire; the reins of their chariots on the day of his preparation [?].
The horsemen will be in turmoil on the roads and will mingle in the squares. Their appearance is like fiery torches, and they run this way and that like lightning.
His nobles will remember and flee by day. They will stumble on their roads and hurry to the walls, and they will prepare their advance guards.
The gates of the cities were opened, and the palaces collapsed.
The possessions were exposed. She was going out, and her maidservants went before her, groaning like doves from their hearts.
The waters of Nineveh were like the waters of a pool, and they fled from you and did not stand their ground, and there was no one who looked.
They seized silver; they seized gold. There was no limit to its adornment; they outweighed all its precious vessels.
Plundering, wrenching, and terror of heart; failing knees and anguish in every waist, and everyone's face like a scorched pot.
Where are the lions' thickets and the prey of their cubs, where the lion went and the lion's cub entered, and there was no one to frighten them?
The lion hunted enough for his cubs and strangled prey for his cubs. He filled his lairs with prey and his dwelling with plunder.

Look, I am against you, says the Lord Almighty. I will burn your multitude in smoke, and the sword will devour your lions. I will remove your prey from the earth, and your deeds will no longer be heard of.
O city of blood, entirely false and full of injustice, whose prey will be searched out!
The sound of blows, the sound of wheels turning, the clatter of chariots, the pounding of horsemen, the flashing of weapons,
the gleaming of swords, the wounded rolling and tumbling about! There was no limit to her nations, and they will grow weak in their bodies because of much prostitution.
A prostitute splendid in beauty, the chief of sorcerers, who sold nations through her prostitution and clans through her sorceries.
Look, I am against you, says the Lord God Almighty. I will expose your backside and throw it over your face. I will show the nations your shame and the kingdoms your dishonor.
I will cast abominations and your filth upon you, and make you a public disgrace.
And everyone who sees you will go down and say, “Alas for you, Nineveh! Who will mourn for you? Where shall we seek comfort for you?”
Prepare a portion; make ready a lyre, the allotted portion of Amon, who lives among rivers, with waters around her, whose beginning is the sea and whose wall is water.
The Ethiopians and Egypt were her strength, and there was no limit to her flight. The Libyans became her helpers.

Yet she too, shaken, will go into captivity. They will dash her children against stones at the beginnings of her roads. They will cast lots over all her honored people, and all her great ones will be bound with their hands in chains.
You too will become drunk and senseless, and you will seek a foothold for yourself against your enemies.
All your strongholds are like a fig-tree lookout: if it is shaken, they will fall into the mouths of those who eat them.
Look, your people within you are like women. The gates of your land will be opened wide to your enemies, and fire will devour your bars.
Fill up water for yourself for the siege, and strengthen your strongholds. Go into the clay and tread it with straw, and make it stronger than brick.
There fire will devour you, and the sword will destroy you. It will devour you like a locust, and it will grow heavy like a locust grub.
You multiplied your merchants like the stars of heaven. The locust grub advanced and flew away.
It moved away like a cricket, and your mixed multitude was like locusts clinging to a fence on a cold day. The sun rose, and it moved away, and its place was no longer known. Woe to them!
Your shepherds have fallen asleep. The king of the Assyrians has slaughtered your forces. Your people have departed to the mountains, and there was no one who remained.
Your wounds have festered, and there is no healing for your brokenness. All who hear the bad news about you will clap their hands over you, for upon whom has your wickedness not come continually?
